gen-dafont-azonix-gf-hind-guntur: Hind Guntur reads tall and stamped-looking, with wide gaps where curves meet stems and no swing between thick and thin. Azonix then takes the heading, a wide-mouthed display face with capitals barely above its lowercase, and it keeps its authority even when shrunk.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-hind-madurai: Wide, stubborn, and a little bossy up top. Hind Madurai follows in a plain sans whose lowercase fills the line like capitals, so Azonix's commanding display letters never have to shout over it.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-hind-mysuru: Contemporary in feel, Hind Mysuru lifts its lowercase tops close to the ascender height and leaves each a slightly ajar. And if Azonix were made small, its wide-mouthed letters would stay crisp, though its commanding presence comes from being left big.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-hind-siliguri: Azonix opens with commanding display letters, its capitals only a hair above the lowercase, so words take a moment to knit together. Hind Siliguri then hums along in a sans of constant line weight, with rounds that gap like a cracked bangle.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-hind-vadodara: Hind Vadodara reads clean and spacious, its rounded glyphs leaving generous gaps at the terminals and its e and a showing tall, open bowls. Azonix holds the heading with authority.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-huninn: Huninn is modern and businesslike. Its lowercase rises close to cap height and its crossbars are as fat as the stems, which gives Azonix's wide, commanding capitals a sturdy partner that stays crisp at any size.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-inter-tight: Rope-like lines, short ascenders, tidy curve tails. Inter Tight handles the text in a modern sans-serif, while Azonix commands the heading with wide-mouthed letters, and that sheer difference in size and attitude is what makes the pair work.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-karla: Karla is stocky and approachable, with a gaping c. Azonix draws its heading like bent copper pipe, authoritative and wide, and Karla sits beneath in a sans with a tall middle band that feels lower and more human.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-kedebideri: Kedebideri rises with a skyward x-height and rounded letters that stay open and inviting. Kedebideri handles the reading, while Azonix commands with strokes that carry no thick-thin pulse, wide and authoritative on their own.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-khula: Khula reads modern and neutral in sans-serif, its tall midsection swelling like a brush-pen belly while its curves keep their mouths open. Azonix is the loud one, with neon-tube strokes.
